title: Resizing windows with Per Pixel Transparency causes major visual glitches on Linux
body:
### Tested versions

4.0.stable,  4.6.1.stable, 4.6.3.stable, 4.7.beta5

### System information

Godot v4.6.3.stable - CachyOS Linux #1 SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Wed, 03 Jun 2026 22:05:15 +0000 on Wayland - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 2 monitors - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1080 (nvidia; 580.159.04) - Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-4770K CPU @ 3.50GHz (8 threads) - 31.28 GiB memory

### Issue description

Major visual glitches when resizing a window with Per Pixel Transparency enabled on Linux

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ad34b1af-5e53-47d2-bb60-85c6615279bb

The window rapidly flickers between fully transparent and opaque when resized at "normal" speeds. Resizing the window by moving the handle quickly just turns the window fully transparent.
This issue practically makes transparent windows on Linux unusable imo :(

I have tested on both Wayland and X11, Comparability and Forward+ Renderer with seemingly no difference.

I've also tested on my laptop: Godot v4.6.3.stable - CachyOS Linux #1 SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Wed, 03 Jun 2026 22:05:15 +0000 on Wayland - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 1 monitor - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - Mesa Intel(R) HD Graphics 4400 (HSW GT2) - Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-4510U CPU @ 2.00GHz (4 threads) - 7.63 GiB memory

### Steps to reproduce

1) Create New Project
2) Make sure Display Server is set to default (x11) in project settings
3) Enable Per Pixel Transparency in project setting.
4) Enjoy the seizure-inducing visuals 

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[Window-resizing-issue.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/28757592/Window-resizing-issue.zip)
